record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: In two dimensions, does there exist a local approximation theorem stating that every ground state of a local gapped Hamiltonian can be approximated on finite regions by a translationally invariant PEPS of finite bond dimension; can this be proved assuming only a spectral gap; and can the required bond-dimension bound g(epsilon) be chosen polynomial in 1/epsilon?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a two-dimensional quantum lattice system on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^d$ attached to each site. Let $H = \sum_{x} h_x$ be a translationally invariant, geometrically local Hamiltonian (each $h_x$ supported in a bounded neighborhood of $x$, of uniformly bounded norm), and assume $H$ has a spectral gap $\gamma > 0$ above its (unique) ground state $|\Omega\rangle$ in the thermodynamic limit.

Recall that a translationally invariant Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) of bond dimension $D$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is the state obtained by placing on every edge of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ a maximally entangled pair in $\mathbb{C}^D \otimes \mathbb{C}^D$ and applying at each site a fixed linear map $A:(\mathbb{C}^D)^{\otimes 4}\to\mathbb{C}^d$.

Problem. Prove or disprove the following 2D local approximation theorem: there exists a function $g:(0,1)\to\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every finite region $R\subset\mathbb{Z}^2$, there exists a translationally invariant PEPS $|\Psi_\varepsilon\rangle$ of bond dimension at most $g(\varepsilon)$ whose reduced density matrix on $R$ satisfies
$$\big\|\mathrm{tr}_{R^c}\big(|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|\big) - \mathrm{tr}_{R^c}\big(|\Psi_\varepsilon\rangle\langle\Psi_\varepsilon|\big)\big\|_1 \le \varepsilon.$$

In addition:
(a) Can such a theorem be established assuming only the existence of a spectral gap (without further structural hypotheses such as frustration-freeness)?
(b) Can the bound $g(\varepsilon)$ be taken polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$?
artifact.status_search_result: In one dimension the analogous local approximation theorem is established (Huang, 2019), giving MPS approximations with bond dimension polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$. In two dimensions only partial results exist: area laws have been proven for frustration-free 2D systems (e.g., Anshu-Arad-Gosset 2021), and complexity-theoretic obstacles (#P-hardness of contracting PEPS) are known, but a full local PEPS approximation theorem for ground states of general 2D gapped Hamiltonians, assuming only a spectral gap and with polynomial bond-dimension bound, has not been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Locally accurate MPS approximations for ground states of 1D gapped local Hamiltonians
status_evidence.snippet: In 1D, bond dimension of approximations scales like (k/ε)^{1+o(1)} for ground states of gapped local Hamiltonians.
status_evidence.claim: The 1D analogue of the desired local approximation theorem has been proven with polynomial bond dimension.

status_evidence.title: An area law for 2D frustration-free spin systems
status_evidence.snippet: Area law proved for locally gapped frustration-free 2D Hamiltonians.
status_evidence.claim: In 2D only partial results (area laws) are known, and only under frustration-freeness, not for general gapped Hamiltonians.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of injective projected entangled pair states
status_evidence.snippet: Contracting PEPS is #P-hard, indicating complexity obstacles to ground-state PEPS approximations in 2D.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity barriers suggest the 2D PEPS approximation question remains nontrivial and is not settled.
